title: Peak Hours 2026 for LESCO, IESCO & All DISCOs | Wattlyst
meta: Peak and off-peak hours by season for LESCO, IESCO and other DISCOs from NEPRA's latest schedule found, and what shifting AC, iron and motor use saves.
author: ali-ahmad

breadcrumb.name: Peak Hours LESCO 2026: Peak and Off-Peak Timings for Every DISCO

p: The latest peak-hour schedule we could find on NEPRA's site is the one in its 2023 tariff determination for IESCO. The PITC bill portal (the billing system the government DISCOs share) currently shows only the December to February window, which matches it; the other three seasons below come from the 2023 determination alone. It gives four seasons, each with a 4-hour evening peak.
December to February: peak 5 pm to 9 pm. March to May: peak 6 pm to 10 pm. June to August: peak 7 pm to 11 pm. September to November: peak 6 pm to 10 pm.

This schedule has not been re-confirmed for 2026. An August 2025 news report said NEPRA asked the DISCOs to propose peak hours ending no later than eleven at night; we have not found a decision adopting a new schedule. The time printed on your own ToU bill or your DISCO's notice overrides this page.

sections.h2: Peak hours IESCO, MEPCO and the other DISCOs
p: We expect the same schedule to apply to all ex-WAPDA DISCOs: LESCO, IESCO, MEPCO, GEPCO, FESCO, PESCO, HESCO, SEPCO, QESCO and TESCO. The 2023 determination we found is IESCO's, but the DISCOs bill through the same PITC system, which shows one December to February window for all of them. That is an inference for the other seasons, not a published fact, so check the peak time printed on your own ToU bill.
K-Electric is the exception. It sets and publishes its own peak-hour timings for Karachi, so check K-Electric's schedule or your bill rather than the schedule above.

sections.h2: Off peak hours: when is electricity cheaper?
p: Every hour outside the peak window is off-peak: in June to August that means before 7 pm and after 11 pm, the whole night and the whole day included. An off-peak unit costs Rs 34.53 against Rs 46.85 for a peak unit on the domestic ToU tariff.

sections.h2: Peak hours in summer and winter
p: The peak moves with sunset. In summer (June to August) it is latest, 7 pm to 11 pm, when evening AC use is highest. In winter (December to February) it is earliest, 5 pm to 9 pm, when lights, heaters and geysers come on after dark. Spring and autumn sit in between.

sections.h2: Who pays peak rates: ToU meter rates explained
p: Only connections on a time-of-use meter. NEPRA's domestic tariff puts every connection with a sanctioned load of 5 kW or more on a ToU meter, which records peak and off-peak units separately. A smaller connection on a normal meter pays its slab rate whatever the hour, so shifting use to the night does not change its bill.

A ToU bill has two energy lines, peak units at Rs 46.85 and off-peak units at Rs 34.53, and a fixed charge of Rs 675 per kW on the higher of half the sanctioned load and the MDI. The FC surcharge, quarterly adjustment, fuel adjustment and GST are added after that, as on any bill.

sections.h2: How much you save by shifting AC, iron and motor use
p: Every unit moved out of the peak window saves the gap between Rs 46.85 and Rs 34.53. For the default month, 150 peak and 650 off-peak units cost Rs 29,472; with only 50 units in the peak, the same total costs Rs 28,240.

The easy moves: iron, run the washing machine and fill the water tank with the motor before the peak starts; pre-cool rooms before the peak and raise the AC set point by a degree or two during it; charge UPS batteries off-peak. The ToU calculator above shows the bill for your own peak and off-peak readings.

faq.q: What are the peak hours for LESCO in 2026?
faq.a: Under NEPRA's latest schedule found, from 2023: 5 pm to 9 pm in December to February, 6 pm to 10 pm in March to May, 7 pm to 11 pm in June to August and 6 pm to 10 pm in September to November. It is not yet re-confirmed for 2026; check your bill.

faq.q: What are the peak hours for IESCO and MEPCO?
faq.a: Most likely the same as LESCO. The schedule here is from NEPRA's 2023 IESCO determination; the PITC bill portal, shared by all ex-WAPDA DISCOs, confirms only the December to February window, so check your bill for the other seasons. By the 2023 schedule, in June to August the peak is 7 pm to 11 pm.
Every hour outside the evening peak window, including the whole day and night. Off-peak units cost Rs 34.53 on the domestic ToU tariff.

faq.q: What are the peak hours in winter?
faq.a: 5 pm to 9 pm in December to February under the 2023 schedule, the earliest window of the year.

faq.q: What are the ToU meter rates?
faq.a: Rs 46.85 per peak unit and Rs 34.53 per off-peak unit on the A-1 domestic tariff, plus a fixed charge of Rs 675 per kW on the higher of half the sanctioned load and the MDI.

faq.q: Do peak hours matter if I do not have a ToU meter?
faq.a: No. Below 5 kW sanctioned load the bill is worked out on slab rates whatever the time, so use the normal bill calculator instead.
K-Electric publishes its own peak-hour timings, so check its schedule or your Karachi bill rather than the DISCO schedule on this page.

faq.q: Why is my real bill higher than this estimate when it is over Rs 25,000?
faq.a: A bill of Rs 25,000 or more a month carries advance income tax under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001: 7.5% of the bill for a domestic consumer who is not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List. This calculator leaves it out because it depends on your tax status; check the income tax line on your bill and FBR's current withholding tax card.

key_facts: Under the latest NEPRA schedule found (the 2023 IESCO tariff determination; PITC's bill portal confirms only the December to February window), peak hours are 5 pm to 9 pm in December to February, 6 pm to 10 pm in March to May, 7 pm to 11 pm in June to August and 6 pm to 10 pm in September to November; every other hour is off-peak.
Peak hours change the price only on a time-of-use (ToU) meter, which domestic connections of 5 kW sanctioned load or more must have; smaller connections pay the normal slab rate at any hour.
On the A-1 domestic ToU tariff a peak unit costs Rs 46.85 and an off-peak unit Rs 34.53, so every unit moved out of peak hours saves the difference between the two.
A ToU home using 150 peak and 650 off-peak units pays Rs 29,472 in energy charges; with only 50 of the same units in peak hours the charge falls to Rs 28,240.
K-Electric publishes its own peak-hour timings, so Karachi consumers should check K-Electric's schedule rather than the DISCO one.

Income tax is not in this estimate: under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, a home not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays advance income tax of 7.5% on a monthly bill of Rs 25,000 or more; consumers on the list pay none.
mistakes: Shifting use to the night on a normal meter. Below 5 kW sanctioned load the bill uses slab rates at every hour, so the time of use does not change the price.
Using another DISCO's or K-Electric's timings. K-Electric publishes its own schedule; check the time on your own bill.
Treating this schedule as confirmed for 2026. It is NEPRA's 2023 schedule; a newer one may apply, and your DISCO's notice overrides it.
Forgetting the fixed charge. On a ToU meter it is billed on the higher of half the sanctioned load and the MDI, so a high evening MDI raises it too.

content.answer: Peak hours for LESCO and the other ex-WAPDA DISCOs are 7 pm to 11 pm in June to August and 5 pm to 9 pm in December to February, per NEPRA's 2023 IESCO schedule, not yet re-confirmed for 2026. They matter on time-of-use meters (5 kW and above): energy charge = peak units × Rs 46.85 + off-peak units × Rs 34.53.

formula.text: ToU energy charge = peak units × peak rate + off-peak units × off-peak rate; fixed charge = fixed rate per kW × max(half the sanctioned load, MDI)
lines: peak and off-peak rates = A-1 domestic ToU rates in the NEPRA tariff (data/tariff-pk-2026.json)
peak window = the season's peak hours; every other hour is off-peak
MDI = maximum demand indicator reading in kW
FC surcharge, QTA, FPA and GST are added on the real bill

content.safety: Running the water motor, washing machine or geyser on a timer to beat the peak is fine, but timers and contactors on motor and geyser circuits must be rated for the load and fitted by a licensed electrician.
